quickAnswerHtml: Keawloon is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, in the Sukhumvit 40 / Soi Saengchan area, Phra Khanong, Khlong Toei. Budget around a set meal per table, roughly THB 800-1,000 per head, book through booking only in advance, via Instagram @keawloonbkk → add LINE from the QR code and give your name/party size/date, then confirm with a deposit; call 065-196-4168, and get there via BTS Ekkamai

blocks.html:
Of the four new Bib Gourmand restaurants in Bangkok for 2026, "Keawloon" is probably the one that gets the most excited reaction when you tell people about it, because this isn't a restaurant in the usual sense at all — it's an actual home, down Soi Saengchan off Sukhumvit 40, where Chef Phat opens his door to just a few tables a day. The restaurant is named after his grandmother, "Keawloon," and what's served is genuinely the family's own home cooking, blending two bloodlines — Nakhon Si Thammarat and Sukhothai — served in the family's own well-worn crockery, passed down through generations. Eating here feels less like going to a restaurant and more like showing up at a relative's house where someone happens to cook brilliantly, and that's exactly why Michelin picked it as a new Bib Gourmand for 2026 despite how few guests it can actually seat.

The format is a set meal per table — there's no à la carte menu to pick dishes from one at a time. The chef puts together a full spread based on his grandmother's home recipes, and the fun part is that the menu changes every 2 months, so anyone who goes this month and again four months later will get an entirely different spread. Budget runs roughly THB 800-1,000 per head and up (one example from a real review: a set for 8 people came to about THB 6,930), which, weighed against the intention behind the food and the experience of eating inside someone's actual home, is a price you can mention to a friend without any need to justify it. The vibe is relaxed home dining — no need to stress over what to wear.

One thing worth knowing before you set your heart on going: Keawloon has the fewest seats of any restaurant on the 2026 Bib Gourmand list — open just twice a day, around noon and 6pm, with only 2-3 tables per seating, and bookings only taken in groups of 2-8 per table. Booking goes through Instagram @keawloonbkk, then adding LINE from the QR code with your name, party size, and date, plus a deposit once confirmed. Seats fill up fast every time the restaurant opens a new month's booking window, and missing that window can mean waiting a month for the next one. But that difficulty is exactly what makes the meal, once you land it, feel like it carries real weight — every table in that house is there because they truly wanted to be.

blocks.descHtml:
Keawloon is a home-cooking restaurant inside an actual house down Soi Saengchan off Sukhumvit 40, about a 12-minute walk from BTS Ekkamai. It serves a set meal per table, budget roughly THB 800-1,000 per head and up (a real example: a set for 8 people ran about THB 6,930). The menu and price change every 2 months, so always check IG before booking. The restaurant is open twice a day, around 12:00 and 18:00, and takes only 2-3 tables per seating — making it the restaurant with the fewest seats on the entire 2026 Bib Gourmand list.

Booking is by advance reservation only, starting on Instagram @keawloonbkk, then adding LINE from the QR code with your name, party size, and date. Once confirmed, you'll need to put down a deposit (you can also call 065-196-4168). The restaurant takes groups of 2-8 per table, and seats fill up fast every time a new month's booking window opens. The trick is to follow the IG account so you can message LINE the moment a new window is announced — otherwise you may be waiting a month. Dress is casual, since you're eating inside someone's home.

faq.q: How do I book Keawloon, and how fast do I need to move?
faq.a: Booking only in advance, via Instagram @keawloonbkk, then adding LINE from the QR code with your name/party size/date. Once confirmed you'll need to put down a deposit (call 065-196-4168). The restaurant takes only 2-3 tables per seating, and seats fill up fast after each month's booking window opens — the moment you see the announcement on IG, message LINE right away
It's a set meal per table, roughly THB 800-1,000 per head and up (example from a review: a set for 8 people ran about THB 6,930). The menu and price change every 2 months, so check IG before booking

You don't choose anything — the restaurant puts together a full grandmother's home-recipe set, blending Nakhon Si Thammarat and Sukhothai cooking, served in the family's own well-worn crockery, and the menu changes every 2 months

faq.q: How do I get there, and what time should I go?
faq.a: The restaurant is at 21/3 Soi Saengchan, Sukhumvit 40, about a 12-minute walk from BTS Ekkamai. It's open twice a day, around 12:00 and 18:00, at whichever time you booked. It takes groups of 2-8 per table, and you can dress casually since you're eating inside a house
